patch_description: Replace the final bilateral one-pole damper with a fixed-λ Whittaker–Henderson polish (second-order difference penalty) solved via a banded O(n) Cholesky solve. The one-pole damper's position-dependent effective smoothing (its exponential memory makes the penalty non-uniform) leaks residual ripple — the slope-change count of 20.4 is the weakest smoothness metric. A constant λ with a second-order difference penalty applies a uniform curvature penalty whose passband is flatter in the band of interest, cutting residual ripple without the lag a stronger one-pole cascade would add. λ is derived from the residual MAD already computed (r_std) and the robust noise scale (sigma_r): clip(25·(r_std/σ_r)², 1, 200). The Whittaker system is pentadiagonal (bandwidth 2 per side), solved in O(n) with a simple banded Cholesky implementation, keeping runtime ≈0.05s. Applied to the full-length signal before the final slice, so the `len(y) = n − window_size + 1` contract is preserved.
